questions.question: Ashima borrowed Rs. 75,000 from a nationalised bank on 26th March 2022 at the rate of 9% per annum simple interest. If she cleared the account on 7th June of the same year, then what amount did she pay?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 75,000 , rate of interest = 9%

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = P × R × T / 100 [ P = principal, R = rate of interest, T = time]

**Calculation**: 

Here total number of days will be 73 days

The simple interest for those 73 days is 

 SI = (75,000 × 9 × 73)/(365 × 100)

⇒ 150 × 9 = Rs 1350

Total amount to be paid 75000 + 1350 = Rs 76350

**∴ The correct option is 2**

Which of the following statement is correct?

I. The ratio of combined sales of P in years A and B to that of combined sales of Q in years D and E is 1 ∶ 2.

II. The sales of P in year C is 300% of the sales of Q in year D.

4e
questions.solution:
**Given**

Sales of P in years A and B: 100, 200

Sales of Q in years D and E: 100, 50

Sales of P in year C = 300

Sales of Q in year D = 100

Concept: We'll calculate the required ratios and percentages and compare with the given statements.

**Solution:**

Combined sales of P in years A and B = 100 + 200 = 300

Combined sales of Q in years D and E = 100 + 50 = 150

Ratio of combined sales of P in years A and B to that of combined sales of Q in years D and E = 300/150 = 2 : 1

Sales of P in year C is 300% of the sales of Q in year D = 3 × 100 = 300.

**Therefore, Statement II is correct, but Statement I is not correct.**

questions.question:
The following bar graph shows the sales (in thousands) of motor bikes by the factories, F1, F2, F3, and F4 in 2017, 2018 and 2019.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d7986c8c9c71fb7235f0b57f1e357645070600d23245f62563019c3c55960f7.png] 

Which factory had the highest sales across all the years ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sales (in thousands) of motor bikes by the factories F1, F2, F3, and F4 in 2017, 2018 and 2019

**Calculation:**

Sales of motor bike by Factory is the Sum of the number of 2017, 2018 and 2019 sales

Sum = Number of motor bike in 2017 + Number of motor bike in 2018 + Number of motor bike 2019

⇒ F1 is sales across all year = 65 + 72 + 83 = 220

⇒ F2 is sales across all year = 69 +71 +73 = 213

⇒ F3 is sales across all year = 58 +64 + 69 = 191

⇒ F4 is sales across all year = 63 + 68 + 69 = 200

**Therefor, Highest sales across all years (2017, 2018 & 2019) is F1**
